title: Speaking practice (hard): Observatory visitor centre and homes
author: toefl-claude-test-generator
description: Listen and repeat with an observatory visitor centre coordinator (long sentences built on articles, each/number-of agreement, collocations, passives and relative clauses); an interview on homes and living spaces that requires describing, past narration, comparing and justifying a choice, and explaining and predicting a trend.

tasks.setting: You are starting work at the visitor centre of a hilltop observatory. Listen to the visitor coordinator and repeat exactly what you hear.

items.text: Each of the telescopes has its own cover.
The number of visitors has doubled since the new exhibition opened.
If the sky is cloudy, we show a short film about the planets instead.
The mirror in the largest telescope, which was polished by hand, has to be cleaned once a year.
Guests who've booked the late tour should be reminded that the car park closes at midnight.
The comet that the staff had been tracking for weeks was finally visible to the naked eye on Friday.

tasks.topic: Homes and the places we live
tasks.intro: Hi, and thanks for joining me. I'm talking to people about their homes and how the places we live shape our everyday lives.

questions.text: To start, could you describe the place where you live now and tell me what you like most about it?
Tell me about a time when you moved to a new home, redesigned a room, or helped someone settle into a new place. What happened, and how did it turn out?
Some people would rather live in a small flat in the city centre, while others prefer a larger house further from the city. Compare the two options, and explain which one you would choose and why.

In many countries, young adults are living with their parents or sharing homes with friends for longer than in the past. Why do you think this is happening, and how might it change the way people live in twenty years?
